topic.label: Archaeology
topic.desc: Archaeology: the study of the human past through material remains, excavation, dating and spatial analysis.

concepts: Locating sites through pedestrian survey, aerial and satellite imagery, lidar and geophysics, managed in GIS.
Controlled excavation, context recording and stratigraphic sequencing of deposits.
Relative and absolute dating methods, including seriation, radiocarbon, dendrochronology and luminescence.
Classification and analysis of lithics, ceramics, metals and other artifacts for technology and exchange.
Human remains, animal bones and plant remains used to reconstruct diet, health and environment.
Interpretive frameworks and the ethics and law of cultural heritage management.
skills: Maps survey results and candidate sites in GIS and checks predicted locations against known site records.
Interprets lidar and satellite imagery for features and checks each identification by ground truth or second review.
Plans magnetometry or ground-penetrating radar survey grids and checks coverage and resolution against targets.
Records excavation contexts with standard forms and checks completeness and consistency of the record.
Builds a Harris matrix from stratigraphic relationships and checks it for cycles and contradictions.
Designs trench placement and sampling for research questions and checks the plan against survey data and literature.
Calibrates radiocarbon ages with a current curve and checks the ranges with Bayesian modeling against stratigraphy.
Orders assemblages by seriation and checks the sequence against independent absolute dates.
Synthesises a regional chronology from published dates and checks it for outliers and source quality.
Classifies ceramic sherds by fabric and form and checks classification against reference collections.
Analyses lithic reduction sequences and checks interpretations against experimental and published data.
Interprets compositional provenance data for artifacts and checks exchange routes on a map against source locations.
Reconstructs diet and mobility from stable isotope values and checks them against regional baselines.
Quantifies animal bone assemblages and checks counts and taphonomy with standard indices.
Assesses health indicators on human remains and checks diagnoses against bioarchaeology literature.
Compares processual and post-processual interpretations of a site and checks arguments against evidence.
Assesses development impacts on heritage sites using GIS and checks the assessment against legal and ethics standards.
Reviews repatriation claims and community consultation and checks them against law and ethics codes.
